paragraphs: Yehudah the tailor. R. Shimon son of Rabbi recited a section before Rabbi. Rabbi said, “How straight this writing is!” Shimon answered, “Yehudah the tailor wrote it.” [In the checked Bavli the section is from Psalms, and Shimon first says he did not write it.] Rabbi told him, “Desist from this evil speech”: Bava Batra 164b. One should never tell a colleague's praise, since praise leads to disparagement. See there and Rav Dimi, Rav Safra's brother. Semag, negative commandment 9, explains: do not praise him before his enemy. But how could Rabbi say “Desist from evil speech,” when Rabbi was not Yehudah the tailor's enemy? One cannot say Rabbi warned his son not to become accustomed to praise, lest he sometimes praise before an enemy: that too is difficult. Whence Semag's explanation? Perhaps even before his friend he should not praise, as Rashbam there and Rashi, Arakhin 16, seem to imply.
